title: Asking questions about types
description:
Class templates can be **partially specialized**: you provide a different version for a whole family of types, such as "any pointer" or "any vector". This is how the standard library's type traits are built.

Write two class templates.

`TypeName<T>` with a `static constexpr std::string_view value`:

| T | value |
|---|---|
| `int` | `"int"` |
| `double` | `"double"` |
| any pointer `U*` | `"pointer"` |
| any `std::vector<U>` | `"vector"` |
| anything else | `"other"` |

`IsPointer<T>` with a `static constexpr bool value`: `true` for any pointer type, `false` otherwise.
hints: Write the general version first (`"other"`, `false`), then a full specialization for each exact type (`template <> struct TypeName<int>`), then partial ones for families: `template <typename U> struct TypeName<U*>` and `template <typename U> struct TypeName<std::vector<U>>`.
Each version has its own `static constexpr` member with the answer.
